Hallmarks of senescence in systemic and pulmonary immunity

Hallmarks of senescence in systemic and pulmonary immunity. The figure summarizes key age-related alterations in innate and adaptive immunity in aged individuals. Innate immune cell changes: Macrophages. Exhibit heightened pro-inflammatory cytokine production and excessive ROS release, defective phagocytosis, and impaired antigen presentation. Neutrophils. Display impaired chemotaxis, aberrant migration, and dysfunctional NET formation. Adaptive immune cell changes: T cells. Phenotypic shifts from naïve to memory T cells occur, with a Th1/Th2 imbalance favoring Th2 predominance, increased Th17 cells, and decreased Tregs, which can reverse upon stimulation. Senescent T cells lack costimulatory molecules (CD27/CD28) but express markers like KLRG-1 and CD57, along with upregulated p16 and p21 and immune checkpoint molecules (Tim-3, TIGIT, CTLA-4). The cells overproduce proinflammatory cytokines (IFN-γ, TNF-α) and cytotoxic mediators (granzyme B, perforin), contributing to aberrant immune responses, functional suppression, tissue damage, defective B cell help, and mitochondrial dysfunction. In the aged lung, IFN-γ signaling further drives T cell activation. B cells. Immunosenescence is characterized by reduced output of mature B cells, expansion of proinflammatory age-associated B cells and double negative B cells, declined CSR and SHM, and impaired germinal center function, resulting in defective antibody production and function. Inflammaging microenvironment. The SASP, activated via p21Cip1, triggers the p38 MAPK and JAK signaling pathways, leading to NF-κB activation and secretion of pro-inflammatory cytokines (IL-1β, IL-6, TNF-α), growth factors (VEGF, TGF-β), chemokines (CXCL1, CXCL8, CCL2), and MMPs (MMP-2, MMP-9). This disrupts the lung microenvironment, promoting chronic inflammation and tissue damage. ROS reactive oxygen species, NET neutrophil extracellular traps, Th T helper cell, Treg regulatory T cell, CD cluster of differentiation, KLRG-1 killer cell lectin-like receptor subfamily G member 1, Tim-3 T cell immunoglobulin and mucin domain-containing protein 3, TIGIT T cell immunoreceptor with Ig and ITIM domains, CTLA-4 cytotoxic T lymphocyte-associated protein 4, IFN-γ interferon gamma, TNF-α tumor necrosis factor alpha, CSR class switch recombination, SHM somatic hypermutation, SASP senescence-associated secretory phenotype, MAPK mitogen-activated protein kinase, JAK Janus kinase, NF-κB nuclear factor kappa-light-chain-enhancer of activated B cells, IL interleukin, VEGF vascular endothelial growth factor, TGF-β transforming growth factor beta, CXCL C-X-C motif chemokine ligand, CCL C-C motif chemokine ligand, MMP matrix metalloproteinase
